evals.prompt: That workflow we just went through for rotating the API credentials was painful to figure out. Turn it into a skill so future sessions get it right.
evals.expected_output: Extracts the intent and the observed failure from the conversation itself as the baseline — what an agent got wrong without guidance, documented concretely — before writing anything. Runs the placement decision: checks whether the fix belongs in a validator or gate, an owning AGENTS.md, or an existing skill before creating a new one, and states why the chosen destination wins. Only then designs the skill, with eval cases planned against the documented baseline.

evals.prompt: Add a new section to the router of our existing review skill covering how to handle generated files. Should be quick — just append it at the end.
evals.expected_output: Refuses the quick append: a router addition changes every behavior in the file. Checks the skill's evals.json for load-bearing lines first, prefers strengthening an existing section or placing the depth in a reference routed by when-to-read, applies the replace-not-append rule if the router is past budget, and requires updating the skill's full eval set for CI to run — not just a case about generated files — without invoking the eval harness locally.

evals.prompt: Write the description for my new skill so it lists the main workflow steps — that way the agent knows what to do even from the listing.
evals.expected_output: Refuses the workflow summary: a description that sketches the process becomes a shortcut the agent follows instead of reading the body, silently dropping the rules that live there. Writes a trigger-only description — symptoms, situations, artifact names, and the do-not-use boundary — and keeps the workflow in the router, honoring the tree's guard sentence and character budget where they apply.

evals.prompt: We need five small skills for the team by end of day. They're all simple, so write them in one batch and we'll test them later once people start using them.
evals.expected_output: Refuses the batch: no skill ships without its baseline failure observed first by hand and eval cases written to prove the change, because an untested skill is untested code and production use is not a test plan. Does not offer to run the eval harness locally — its execution is deferred to CI. Proceeds one skill at a time — observe, write, cover with cases, wire — and states that simplicity is a rationalization, not an exemption.

evals.prompt: Audit this skill for us. Report what is wrong with it; do not edit anything.
evals.expected_output: Read-only audit naming defects by layer with fixes: the description summarizes the workflow and baits overtriggering with unrelated DevOps scope; the router explains concepts any agent knows, summarizes its own reference into a table of contents plus an in-short recap, stacks capitalized musts including a nuance clause (skip canary unless it matters less) and an exemption clause about code blocks that does not scope; the examples repeat one pattern in three languages; the notes section is a narrative war story; and the skill ships no evals, so nothing proves it changes behavior. Does not edit the fixture.
